claims.claim: Iranian forces destroyed two U.S. transport aircraft and two Black Hawks during a failed pilot-rescue mission.
claims.supported: Iranian fire hit rescue helicopters; U.S. aircraft were lost inside Iran.
claims.not_supported: The rescue did not fail; both F-15E crew were recovered. Reuters reports the two disabled MC-130s and additional helicopters were destroyed by U.S. forces after mechanical/operational problems to prevent capture. The reviewed evidence does not support Iran-caused destruction of all claimed aircraft.
inference_basis: Iranian fire hit rescue helicopters; U.S. aircraft were lost inside Iran. The rescue did not fail; both F-15E crew were recovered. Reuters reports the two disabled MC-130s and additional helicopters were destroyed by U.S. forces after mechanical/operational problems to prevent capture. The reviewed evidence does not support Iran-caused destruction of all claimed aircraft.
evidence_that_would_change_assessment: New independent physical evidence, primary records, or later operational behavior materially inconsistent with the present inference.

claims.claim: The April rescue operation was actually a U.S. mission to steal Iran’s enriched uranium.
claims.supported: The U.S. military had separately drafted, at Trump’s request, a contingency plan to seize Iranian enriched uranium.
claims.not_supported: No reviewed evidence connects that contingency plan operationally to the April 3-5 rescue. The public contingency concept described by the Washington Post would require excavation, nuclear specialists, major logistics, and potentially weeks/months—substantially different from the documented personnel-recovery mission.
inference_basis: The U.S. military had separately drafted, at Trump’s request, a contingency plan to seize Iranian enriched uranium. No reviewed evidence connects that contingency plan operationally to the April 3-5 rescue. The public contingency concept described by the Washington Post would require excavation, nuclear specialists, major logistics, and potentially weeks/months—substantially different from the documented personnel-recovery mission.
credible_alternatives: A covert secondary objective is theoretically possible, but no operation-specific evidence supports it.
evidence_that_would_change_assessment: New independent physical evidence, primary records, or later operational behavior materially inconsistent with the present inference.

claims.claim: The Iranian F-5 pilots associated with the Camp Buehring mission were shot down/killed.
claims.supported: Iran did lose F-5 aircraft in separate strikes during the war.
claims.not_supported: The three pilots claiming the Camp Buehring mission appeared alive in an Iranian state-TV interview on June 17. Separate events include Israeli destruction of F-5/F-4 aircraft at Tabriz, U.S. destruction of other F-5s at Ahvaz, and Qatar shooting down two Iranian Su-24s.
inference_basis: The three pilots publicly identified as the Camp Buehring mission participants appeared alive on Iranian state TV on June 17.
Separate Iranian F-5 losses do not establish deaths of those named mission participants.
credible_alternatives: A different F-5 crew could have been killed in a separate event, but that would not validate the claim about these three pilots.
evidence_that_would_change_assessment: Verified casualty records showing one of the three interviewed pilots was not the person claimed or that the interview was misidentified/fabricated.

claims.claim: Iran admitted on live TV that it was the side that broke the April ceasefire by firing first.
claims.supported: Iranian state broadcaster confirmed the June 7 launches; they were the first direct Iran-to-Israel missile bombardment since the April ceasefire. IRGC publicly described the strike as retaliation.
claims.not_supported: The reviewed evidence does not establish a specific live-TV interview admitting Iran was first to violate every term of the April ceasefire. The June 7 Iranian strike followed an Israeli strike in Beirut. Iran treated attacks on Lebanon/resistance forces as ceasefire violations, while a later Iranian account itself acknowledged Lebanon was not explicitly covered. Scope was contested.
inference_basis: Iranian state media confirms the June 7 launches and their retaliatory framing.
The exact claimed live-TV admission has not been recovered.
An Israeli strike in Beirut preceded the Iranian launch and ceasefire scope regarding Lebanon was disputed.
credible_alternatives: A still-unrecovered interview may contain narrower wording that was later paraphrased as an admission.
evidence_that_would_change_assessment: Primary video/transcript containing an explicit Iranian admission that its June 7 action was the first violation of the governing ceasefire terms.

method_rule: Summary layer only. Canonical adjudication is iranian-claim-evolution.json; final_disposition values use controlled vocabulary. Superseding doctrine: each consequential case also carries a separate estimative judgment; UNRESOLVED is used only when live explanations remain roughly balanced.
